{{Short description|Classic counterexample in topology}}
[[File:Infinite broom.svg|right|thumb|Standard infinite broom]]
In [[topology]], a branch of [[mathematics]], the '''infinite broom''' is a [[subset]] of the [[Euclidean plane]] that is used as an example distinguishing various notions of [[Connected space|connectedness]]. The '''closed infinite broom''' is the [[Closure (topology)|closure]] of the infinite broom, and is also referred to as the '''broom space'''.<ref>Chapter 6 exercise 3.5 of {{Citation |last=Joshi |first=K. D. |year=1983 |title=Introduction to general topology |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |location=New York |isbn=978-0-85226-444-7 |mr=0709260}}</ref>

==Definition==
The infinite broom is the subset of the Euclidean plane that consists of all [[closed line segment]]s joining the [[Origin (mathematics)|origin]] to the point {{nowrap|(1, 1/''n'')}} as ''n'' varies over all [[positive integer]]s, together with the [[interval (mathematics)|interval]] (½, 1] on the ''x''-axis.<ref name=CIT>{{Citation |last1=Steen |first1=Lynn Arthur |author1-link=Lynn Arthur Steen |last2=Seebach |first2=J. Arthur Jr |author2-link=J. Arthur Seebach, Jr. |year=1995 |title=[[Counterexamples in Topology]] |edition=[[Dover Publications|Dover]] reprint of 1978 |orig-year=First published 1978 |publisher=Dover Publications |location=Mineola, NY |page=139 |isbn=978-0-486-68735-3 |mr=1382863}}</ref>

The closed infinite broom is then the infinite broom together with the interval (0, ½] on the ''x''-axis. In other words, it consists of all closed line segments joining the origin to the point {{nowrap|(1, 1/''n'')}} or to the point {{nowrap|(1, 0)}}.<ref name=CIT />

==Properties==
Both the infinite broom and its closure are [[Connected space|connected]], as every [[open set]] in the plane which contains the segment on the ''x''-axis must intersect slanted segments. Neither is [[locally connected]]. Despite the closed infinite broom being [[arc connected]], the standard infinite broom is not [[path connected]].<ref name=CIT />

The interval [0,1] on the ''x''-axis is a [[Retraction (topology)#Deformation retract and strong deformation retract|deformation retract]] of the closed infinite broom, but it is not a ''strong'' deformation retract.
